newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain forecasts sharp drop in 97/98 deficit.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain forecasts sharp drop in 97/98 deficit.

text.p: Bahrain projected on Sunday a 75 million dinar ($199 million) deficit in its two-year 1997/1998 budget, down from a projected 236 million dinars in the 1996/1997 budget.

Cabinet Affairs and Information Minister Mohammad Ibrahim al-Mutawae, quoted by the official Gulf News Agency, said the "total budget for the financial 1997 and 1998 years amounted to 1.395 billion dinars".

Mutawae, speaking after a regular cabinet meeting, said the oil-rich island nation would finance the 75 million dinar deficit from loans by Arab investment funds, the Islamic Development Bank and national financing sources, in apparent reference to government bonds and treasury bills.

Mutawae said Bahrain planned to cut the deficit to around 3.5 percent of its gross domestic product in the 1997/1998 budget from a previous 8.5 percent "as part of a new financial policy for the next 10 years to wipe out the deficit".
He did not say how Bahrain planned to cut its deficit.
He said the plan also aimed to increase national income, raise the standard of living and strengthen Bahrain's financial and economic position.

Bahrain produces around 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) of oil from its own fields and receives full production of 140,000 bpd from a joint oilfield with Saudi Arabia. It also imports 200,000 bpd from the kingdom for refining.
